preconditions.description: The number of users n is an integer between 2 and 250,000 inclusive.
Both T1 and T2 contain exactly n-1 edges.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in T1_edges) and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in T2_edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints in both trees are valid user indices between 1 and n.
Both edge sets form a valid tree structure on n vertices.

postconditions.description: The printed count m equals the number of matched pairs in the output.

postconditions.expression: all((u1, v1) in T1_edges_set for (u1, v1, u2, v2) in matched_pairs) and all((u2, v2) in T2_edges_set for (u1, v1, u2, v2) in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: Every edge in the output pairs belongs to the respective input tree T1 or T2.

postconditions.expression: len({(u1, v1) for (u1, v1, u2, v2) in matched_pairs}) == m and len({(u2, v2) for (u1, v1, u2, v2) in matched_pairs}) == m
postconditions.description: All T1 edges in the pairs are distinct, and all T2 edges in the pairs are distinct.

postconditions.expression: all(is_connected_after_swap(n, T1_edges, e1, e2) for e1, e2 in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: For every pair (e1, e2), removing e1 from T1 and adding e2 results in a connected graph (a tree).

postconditions.expression: not any(len(matched_pairs) < len(candidate_pairs) and all(is_connected_after_swap(n, T1_edges, e1, e2) for e1, e2 in candidate_pairs) and len({e1 for e1, e2 in candidate_pairs}) == len(candidate_pairs) and len({e2 for e1, e2 in candidate_pairs}) == len(candidate_pairs) for candidate_pairs in all_valid_matchings(n, T1_edges, T2_edges))
postconditions.description: The set of matched pairs represents a maximum matching in the bipartite graph defined by valid replacements.
